motif.name: Rest
motif.description: Passages of the piano score that match one melody, in levels by how close they are to it. Level 1 is the closest. A run of repeated notes counts as one note. Passages that overlap, or lie within 1 measure of each other, are joined into one; the level is that of the closest.

source.author: J. K. Holman
source.title: Wagner's Ring: A Listener's Companion & Concordance
source.publication: Portland, Oregon: Amadeus Press, 1996; paperback 2003, ISBN 978-1-57467-070-7

levels.label: Original
levels.name: The melody as given
levels.description: The melody as you gave it. It is not a passage of the score.

levels.name: Closest to the original
levels.description: The best partial matches of the whole phrase. The pitches and the rhythm are the same, in any octave.

levels.name: Same core pitches
levels.description: Notes 1 to 13 of the phrase have the same pitches, in any octave, but the rhythm differs. In a sung passage the score may have one short extra note between two of them: it is skipped.

levels.name: One note different
levels.description: Notes 1 to 13 of the phrase have the same pitches, in any octave, except one note. The rhythm may differ.

levels.name: Other keys
levels.description: Notes 1 to 13 of the phrase have the same intervals, moved to another key, in any octave. The rhythm may differ.

levels.name: Opening, other keys
levels.description: Only the first notes, 1 to 8 of the phrase, have the same intervals, moved to another key. The rhythm may differ. Short cells also match by chance, so some of these passages are coincidences.

occurrences.label: The original
occurrences.note: The melody as you gave it, engraved from your notes. It has no pickup, the bars are in 4/4, and the score has a treble clef and 4 flats in the key signature. It is not a passage of the score.

libretto.text: Die Weckerin lacht in den Grund.

libretto.translation: Through the waters flows his radiant star!
(a wordless cry)

libretto.translation: You terrible, terrible god!
Terrible god!
Terrible god!

libretto.text: Ach, wende, du Schrecklicher, wende, ach wende von ihr diese schreiende Schmach, wend' ab die Schmach!
libretto.translation: Oh, turn, you terrible one, turn, oh turn this crying shame away from her, turn away the shame!

libretto.text: Wende von ihr die schreiende Schmach!
libretto.translation: Turn the crying shame from her!

libretto.text: Wende von ihr die schreiende Schmach!
libretto.translation: Turn the crying shame from her!

libretto.text: Wende von ihr die schreiende Schmach; schrecklicher, wende von ihr die schreiende Schmach! Ach wende die Schmach!
libretto.translation: Turn the crying shame from her; terrible one, turn the crying shame from her! Oh turn away the shame!

libretto.text: Ach wende von ihr die schreckliche Schmach!
libretto.translation: Oh, turn the terrible shame away from her!

libretto.text: Wende die Schmach! Schrecklicher, Ach wende, wende die Schmachvon ihr!
libretto.translation: Turn away the shame! Terrible one, oh turn, turn the shame from her!

libretto.text: Ach wende ab die Schmach! Ach, wende, du Schrecklicher, wende, ach wende von ihr diese schreiende Schmach, ach wende die Schmach, ach wende, wende die Schmach!
libretto.translation: Oh, avert the shame! Oh, turn it away, you terrible one, turn, oh turn this crying shame away from her, oh turn away the shame, oh turn, turn away the shame!

libretto.text: Ach wende die Schmach! Ach, wende die schreiende Schmach! Wende die Schmach! Ach wende, Schrecklicher, die Schmach! Ach wende, wende die Schmach!
libretto.translation: Oh, turn away the shame! Oh, turn away the crying shame! Turn away the shame! Oh turn, terrible one, the shame! Oh turn, turn away the shame!

libretto.text: wende die Schmach! schrecklicher, wende, ach wende die schreiende Schmach von ihr! Ach wende, wende die Schmach!
libretto.translation: turn away the shame! terrible one, turn, oh turn the crying shame from her! Oh turn, turn away the shame!

libretto.text: Wende die Schmach! Schrecklicher, ach wende die Schmach!
libretto.translation: Turn away the shame! Terrible one, oh turn away the shame!

libretto.text: Wie die Schwester träf' uns auch ihr Schimpf, wie die Schwester träf' uns selbst auch ihr Schimpf!
libretto.translation: Like the sister, their disgrace would strike us too, like the sister, their disgrace would strike even ourselves!

libretto.text: Wie die Schwester träf' uns auch der Schimpf,
libretto.translation: Like the sister, the disgrace would strike us too,

libretto.text: Wie die Schwester träfe uns selber der Schimpf,
libretto.translation: Like the sister, the disgrace would strike us ourselves,

libretto.text: Wie die Jungen den Alten gleichen,
libretto.translation: How the young resemble the old,

libretto.text: das hab’ ich mir glücklich ersehn.
libretto.translation: I have happily picked that out for myself.

libretto.text: Nun kam ich zum klaren Bach:
libretto.translation: Now I came to the clear brook:

libretto.text: da erspäht’ ich die Bäum’ und Tier’ im Spiegel;
libretto.translation: then I spied the trees and animals in the mirror;

libretto.text: Sonn’ und Wolken, wie sie nur sind,
libretto.translation: sun and clouds, just as they are,
in the glitter they appeared alike.

libretto.text: Da sah ich denn auch mein eigen Bild: –
libretto.translation: Then I saw my own image too: –

libretto.text: So nützt’ ihm des Blutes Genuß.
libretto.translation: So the tasting of the blood benefited him.

libretto.text: Er sinnt und erwägt der Beute Wert: –
libretto.translation: He ponders and weighs the value of the booty: –

libretto.text: weilte wohl hier ein weiser Wandrer,
libretto.translation: perhaps a wise wanderer stayed here,
roamed about, talked the child round
with cunning advice of runes?

libretto.text: Zwiefach schlau sei nun der Zwerg;
libretto.translation: Let the dwarf now be doubly cunning;

libretto.text: die listigste Schlinge leg’ ich jetzt aus,
libretto.translation: I now lay out the craftiest snare,
so that with intimate deceitful talk
beguile the defiant child.

libretto.translation: The hovering ardor pleased me.
Did Brünnhilde take you for Gunther?

libretto.text: Ihm glich ich auf ein Haar:
libretto.translation: I resembled him to a hair:
the Tarnhelm did that,
as Hagen ably showed.
I gave you good advice.

libretto.text: Auf den Ästen saß es und sang:
libretto.translation: It sat on the branches and sang:
«Hey! Siegfried now owns
the Niblungs' hoard!
Oh! if he found in the cave
the hoard now!
If he wanted to win the Tarnhelm,

libretto.text: der taugt’ ihm zu wonniger Tat!
libretto.translation: it would serve him for blissful deeds!

libretto.text: doch wollt’ er den Ring sich erraten,
libretto.translation: but he wanted to guess the ring for himself,

libretto.text: der macht’ ihn zum Walter der Welt!»
libretto.translation: that made him ruler of the world!»

libretto.text: Ring und Tarnhelm trugst du nun fort?
libretto.translation: Ring and Tarnhelm you carried off now?
Did you hear the little bird again?

libretto.text: Ring und Tarnhelm hatt’ ich gerafft:
libretto.translation: I had snatched up ring and Tarnhelm:

libretto.text: da lauscht’ ich wieder dem wonnigen Laller;
libretto.translation: then I listened again to the blissful babbler;

libretto.text: der saß im Wipfel und sang:
libretto.translation: who sat in the treetop and sang:

libretto.text: «Hei! Siegfried gehört nun der Helm und der Ring.
libretto.translation: «Hey! Siegfried now owns the helmet and the ring.

libretto.text: Oh! traute er Mime, dem treulosen, nicht!
libretto.translation: Oh, let him not trust Mime, the faithless one!

libretto.text: Ihm sollt’ er den Hort nur erheben;
libretto.translation: He was only to raise the hoard for him;

libretto.text: nun lauert er listig am Weg;
libretto.translation: now he lurks cunningly by the way;

libretto.text: nach dem Leben trachtet er Siegfried:
libretto.translation: he seeks Siegfried's life:
oh, Siegfried, do not trust Mime!»
He reminded you well?

libretto.text: da saß es noch und sang:
libretto.translation: there it still sat and sang:

libretto.text: «Hei, Siegfried erschlug nun den schlimmen Zwerg!
libretto.translation: «Hey, Siegfried has now slain the wicked dwarf!

libretto.text: Jetzt wüßt’ ich ihm noch das herrlichste Weib;
libretto.translation: Now I know for him yet the most glorious woman;
she sleeps on a high rock,
Fire burns around her hall:
